name: Little Shanghai Bok Choy
guide: Mini pac choi; thin to one plant and keep cool. Cut the compact head or harvest outer stalks while the center keeps growing.

name: Benary's Giant Mix Zinnia
guide: Tall cut-flower mix; give high light and room for branching. Cut blooms just before fully open; move outdoors if it crowds the tower.

name: Black Viola
guide: Compact dark blooms; keep cool and deadhead fading flowers to renew buds. Pick open flowers for garnish; leave seeds covered to germinate.

name: Blush Hibiscus
guide: Large, slow blooms; support tall stems and trim roots twice monthly. Remove faded flowers and pick young leaves or freshly opened blooms.

name: Cheyenne Spirit Echinacea
guide: Tall, slow perennial; give high light and room or transplant outdoors. Cut open blooms for flowers; indoor Gardyn performance is unverified.

name: Durango Outback Mix Marigold
guide: Compact French marigold; deadhead spent blooms to keep buds coming. Pick open flowers and remove petals from the bitter flower base.

name: Fiesta Gitana
guide: Dwarf calendula; pinch tall shoots and remove spent flowers with their bare stems. Cut half-open blooms or pick fresh petals for garnish.

name: Flashback Mix Calendula
guide: Edible calendula mix; deadhead spent flowers and pinch tips to keep it bushy. Pick fresh petals or cut partly open blooms for arrangements.

name: Fuchsia Snapdragon
guide: Fuchsia flower spikes; give high light and remove spent blooms to renew buds. Cut stems above a leaf node, leaving a third of the plant.

name: Night-Scented Stock
guide: Evening-scented blooms; deadhead flowers and remove the bare stems. Cut stalks as flowers start opening and place them in water promptly.

name: Oopsy Daisy
guide: Calendula with pale, orange-tipped blooms; pinch tips and deadhead bare stems. Cut partly open flowers or pick petals before they fade.

name: Pink Petunia
guide: Pink ornamental blooms; deadhead and shorten trailing stems while leaving a third. Keep roots trimmed; flowers are not edible.

name: Purple Petunia
guide: Purple ornamental blooms; deadhead and shorten trailing stems while leaving a third. Keep roots trimmed; flowers are not edible.

name: Radio Calendula
guide: Orange calendula blooms; pinch tall stalks and deadhead flowers with their bare stems. Cut half-open blossoms or pick petals while fresh.

name: Scarlet Snapdragon
guide: Scarlet flower spikes; give high light and remove spent blooms. Cut stems above a leaf node, leaving a third of the plant to regrow.

name: Trailing Nasturtium Mix
guide: Long trailing vines; give room or train them away from neighboring plants. Pick young leaves and open flowers, and trim vines to limit spread.

name: Violet Impatiens
guide: Violet ornamental blooms; keep cool and remove spent flowers. Cut back leggy stems while leaving a third of the plant for another flush.

name: White Petunia
guide: White ornamental blooms; deadhead and shorten trailing stems while leaving a third. Keep roots trimmed; flowers are not edible.

name: Yellow Snapdragon
guide: Yellow flower spikes; give high light and remove spent blooms. Cut stems above a leaf node, leaving a third of the plant to regrow.

name: Bare Root Strawberries
guide: Established crowns; plant promptly in high light and hand-pollinate flowers. Remove runners and pick ripe berries; avoid germination mode.

name: Black Pearl Pepper
guide: Dark-leaved ornamental pepper; give high light and warmth, and hand-pollinate flowers. Trim to fit; the small fruit turns red and is hot.

name: Burrito Pepper
guide: Compact hot pepper; give high light and hand-pollinate after removing the first buds. Support fruiting stems and cut firm peppers at the stem.

name: Candy Cane Pepper
guide: Striped sweet pepper; give high light and hand-pollinate after the first buds are removed. Cut firm fruit green-striped or let it ripen red.

name: Fairytale Eggplant
guide: Compact striped eggplant; give high light, hand-pollinate flowers, and support fruiting stems. Cut fruit while the skin is glossy.

name: Goliath Pepper
guide: Large sweet pepper; give high light, hand-pollinate flowers, and support heavy fruit. Cut firm peppers green or let them ripen golden.

name: Purple Beans
guide: Purple bush beans; support stems and help flowers pollinate with a gentle shake. Pick tender pods before seeds swell to prolong production.

name: Super Sugar Snap Pea
guide: Tall snap-pea vine; provide strong support and keep it cool. Pick plump pods before seeds become starchy; allow room or transplant outdoors.

name: Yellow Beans
guide: Compact wax beans; give high light and support fruiting stems. Pick tender yellow pods before seeds swell, harvesting often to keep them coming.

name: Bouquet Dill
guide: Early-flowering dill; snip leafy stems before buds open for the longest leaf harvest. Trim tall growth, or leave umbels to mature for seed.

name: Doron Prospera Basil
guide: Purple Genovese-type basil; pinch above leaf pairs and remove flower buds. Harvest upper stems regularly while leaving enough foliage to regrow.

name: Giant of Italy Parsley
guide: Large flat-leaf parsley; allow time for slow germination. Cut mature outer stems at the base and leave the center to keep producing.

name: Greek Oregano
guide: Pungent oregano; pinch stem tips to encourage branching. Snip established leafy sprigs before flowering and leave enough growth to recover.

name: Kapoor Tulsi (Holy Basil)
guide: Bushy tulsi; give bright light and pinch stem tips to encourage branching. Snip leafy sprigs and remove flower buds to extend leaf harvest.

name: Mammoth Basil
guide: Large, ruffled basil leaves; pinch stems above leaf pairs and remove flower buds. Harvest upper growth often to encourage branching.

name: Summer Thyme
guide: Tender-stemmed thyme; allow time for establishment and pinch tips for branching. Snip leafy sprigs sparingly while young, then harvest regularly.

name: Allstar Gourmet Lettuce Mix
guide: Single-species lettuce mix; keep cool and cut baby leaves above the growing point. Leave the centers intact for another flush.

name: Breen Lettuce
guide: Compact red romaine; keep cool and harvest outer leaves while leaving the center. Cut the whole head at maturity for a single harvest.

name: Bright Lights Swiss Chard
guide: Multicolored chard; harvest outer stalks at the base and leave the crown intact. Pick young leaves for tenderness and check roots monthly.

name: Bronze Arrow Lettuce
guide: Bronze-tinted leaf lettuce; keep cool and snip outer leaves once established. Leave the center growing or cut the whole head at maturity.

name: Cardinale
guide: Red lettuce that forms a crisp head; keep cool to delay bolting. Pick outer leaves while leaving the center, or cut the mature head at its base.

name: Cecelia Lettuce
guide: Compact green butterhead; keep cool and harvest outer leaves or the full head. Listed head-maturity days start at transplant, not sowing.

name: Flashy Trout Back Lettuce
guide: Speckled romaine; keep cool and harvest outer leaves while the center regrows. Cut the mature head at its base; red leaf spots are normal.

name: Green Mustard
guide: Mizuna-type mustard; keep cool and cut young outer leaves while leaving the center. Remove flower stems and check vigorous roots twice monthly.

name: Matilda
guide: Green butter-textured lettuce; keep cool and harvest outer leaves while leaving the center. Cut the full head at maturity and trim roots monthly.

name: Monte Carlo Lettuce
guide: Compact romaine; keep cool and snip outer leaves above the base for repeat harvests. Cut the full head at maturity and leave room for airflow.

name: Pink Celery
guide: Pink-stemmed celery; allow for slow early growth. Cut larger outer stalks at the base and leave a third of the plant to continue producing.

name: Pink Swiss Chard
guide: Pink-stemmed chard; cut outer leaves and stalks at their base, leaving the crown intact. Pick young for tenderness and check roots monthly.

name: Red Lace Mustard
guide: Cut nursery microgreens above the seed pad; cut seedlings will not regrow. For baby greens, transfer uncut plants once roots reach 2 inches.

name: Red Mustard
guide: Red mustard leaves; keep cool and harvest young outer leaves for a milder flavor. Leave the center growing and remove flower stems as they appear.

name: Rouge d'Hiver
guide: Cold-tolerant red romaine; keep cool and harvest outer leaves while leaving the center. Cut the whole head when mature for a single harvest.

name: Ruby Streaks Mustard
guide: Fine, maroon mustard leaves; keep cool and pick young outer growth for a mild bite. Baby leaves are ready before full-size plants.

name: Salanova Green Butter Lettuce
guide: Butter-type Salanova; keep cool and harvest outer leaves or cut around the core. Listed head-maturity days start at transplant, not sowing.

name: Shungiku
guide: Grow as tray microgreens with even moisture and good airflow. Cut above the medium when the first true leaves emerge; timing is for microgreens.

name: Sorrel
guide: Tart green sorrel; snip young outer leaves and leave the crown to regrow. Cut flower stalks to prolong leaf production and keep it compact.

name: Wasabi Greens
guide: Spicy mustard greens; keep cool and pick outer leaves young for a milder bite. Leave the center intact and harvest flowers as they open.
